name: Polybius, plain square, HELLO
ref: standard Polybius square (A = 11 ... Z = 55 without J), the classic HELLO example

example.title: The default square
example.note: H is in row 2 and column 3, so it becomes 23, and E becomes 15. The output has only digits.

name: Polybius decrypt, plain square
ref: standard Polybius square, the classic HELLO example

example.title: Digit pairs back to letters
example.note: Each pair gives a row and a column, so 23 is H and 15 is E, and 2315313134 reads HELLO.

name: Polybius with the keyed square, POLYBIUS CIPHER
ref: Polybius square of Wikipedia "Polybius square" (keyword POLYBIUS CIPHER gives its grid, checked against the article table)

example.title: A key first in the square
example.note: With the key POLYBIUSCIPHER the first letter S becomes 23, where the default square would give 43.

name: Polybius keyed square decrypt
ref: Polybius square of Wikipedia "Polybius square" (keyword POLYBIUS CIPHER gives its grid, checked against the article table)

example.title: The same key is needed
example.note: With the key POLYBIUSCIPHER the pairs read SOMETEXT, so the key must match the one used for encryption.

name: Polybius merges J into I
ref: standard Polybius square

example.title: J is read as I
example.note: J shares a cell with I, so J gives 24 as I does, and JAM becomes 241132.

ref: hand-computed

name: Polybius decrypt of a digit 6 is E_COERCE

name: Nihilist, published example ZEBRAS / RUSSIAN
ref: Nihilist cipher, worked example on Wikipedia (ZEBRAS square, RUSSIAN key, DYNAMITE WINTER PALACE): the article's number list

example.title: A keyed square and a repeating key
example.note: The square is keyed by ZEBRAS and the key RUSSIAN repeats over the letters. The spaces are dropped and the sums are joined by spaces.

name: Nihilist decrypt, published example
ref: Nihilist cipher, worked example on Wikipedia (ZEBRAS square, RUSSIAN key, DYNAMITE WINTER PALACE): the article's number list

example.title: Undo the keyed example
example.note: The key is taken off each number and the rest are read as square cells, giving DYNAMITEWINTERPALACE with no spaces.

name: Nihilist, plain square, key A
ref: hand-computed: H = 23, E = 15, L = 31, O = 34 in the plain square (J omitted), A = 11

example.title: Cell numbers added together
example.note: H is in row 2 and column 3, so 23, and the key letter A is 11. Their sum, 34, is the first number of the output.

name: Nihilist decrypt rejects a number that is no sum of two cells
ref: hand-computed: 99 less key coordinate 14 is 85, not a cell

name: Nihilist rejects a key with a digit
ref: parameter check (key letters only)

name: ADFGX, published example ATTACKATONCE
ref: ADFGX cipher, worked example on Wikipedia (square BTALPDHOZKQFVSNGICUXMREWY, transposition CARGO, plaintext ATTACKATONCE)

example.title: ADFGX with a square and a transposition key
example.note: Each letter becomes two of the labels A, D, F, G and X, then the pairs are rearranged by the key CARGO. The 12 letters give 24 labels.

name: ADFGX decrypt, published example
ref: ADFGX cipher, worked example on Wikipedia (square BTALPDHOZKQFVSNGICUXMREWY, transposition CARGO, plaintext ATTACKATONCE)

example.title: Undo the ADFGX example
example.note: The transposition is undone first, then each pair of labels names a cell, so FAXDFADDDGDGFFFAFAXAFAFX gives ATTACKATONCE again.

name: ADFGX, variant omitted takes adfgx
ref: ADFGX cipher, worked example on Wikipedia (square BTALPDHOZKQFVSNGICUXMREWY, transposition CARGO, plaintext ATTACKATONCE)

name: ADFGVX, published example attack at 1200am
ref: ADFGVX cipher, worked example on Wikipedia (6 by 6 square NA1C3H8TB2OME5WRPD4F6G7I9J0KLQSUVXYZ as the article's grid, transposition PRIVACY, plaintext attack at 1200am)

example.title: ADFGVX also labels the digits
example.note: The 6 by 6 square holds the digits too, so 1200 gets labels and the labels include V. Fourteen letters and digits give 28 labels.

name: ADFGVX decrypt, published example
ref: ADFGVX cipher, worked example on Wikipedia (6 by 6 square NA1C3H8TB2OME5WRPD4F6G7I9J0KLQSUVXYZ as the article's grid, transposition PRIVACY, plaintext attack at 1200am)

example.title: ADFGVX with the 6 by 6 square
example.note: With the variant adfgvx and its own square, the pairs read back as ATTACKAT1200AM, digits included.

name: ADFGX decrypt rejects an odd number of labels
ref: hand-computed: 25 labels, one more than the 24 of the published text

name: ADFGX decrypt rejects a letter that is no label
ref: hand-computed: Z is not a row or column label of ADFGX

name: ADFGX rejects an unknown variant
ref: static check: the variant is a choice of adfgx or adfgvx

example.title: A French proverb in a keyed cube
example.note: Only the letters are kept, so the spaces, the hyphen and the apostrophe are dropped from aide-toi, le ciel t'aidera.

name: Trifid decrypt, published example
ref: Trifid cipher, worked example on Wikipedia (key FELIXMARDELASTELLE, period 5, aide-toi, le ciel t'aidera)

example.title: Undo the French example
example.note: With the same key and period 5, FMJFVOISSUFTFPUFEQQC gives back the letters of the proverb, without spaces or punctuation.

name: Trifid, plain cube and default period 5
ref: hand-computed: plain cube A to Z then +, layers, rows and columns of the first nine letters, period 5

example.title: The 27th symbol is a plus sign
example.note: With no key the cube runs A to Z and then plus, so a plus sign can appear in the output, as it does here.

name: Trifid decrypt reads the 27th symbol +
ref: round trip of the plain-cube vector above

example.title: The plus sign reads back as the 27th symbol
example.note: Decrypting AABKTAF+F with no key gives ABCDEFGHI, so the plus sign is read as the 27th symbol.

name: Trifid rejects period 0
ref: static check: period is 1 to 1000
